title: PLACEHOLDER: Lindenfield Health Partners — claims intake automation
source_material:
PLACEHOLDER — fictional, written for the CCR MCP proof of concept. Lindenfield Health Partners is not a real organisation and none of this happened. Replace with a real, approved case study before testers see it.

DELIVERY LEAD'S SUMMARY (project close-out)

Lindenfield Health Partners is a regional health plan with about 340,000 members. Paper and fax claims were keyed by hand, and a backlog of several weeks was normal at quarter end.

We ran a five-month engagement:
- Document AI to classify and extract fields from faxed and scanned claims, with a human review queue for low-confidence fields.
- Integration with the existing claims adjudication platform through its published APIs.
- Training for the intake team, who moved from keying to reviewing exceptions.

MEASURED RESULTS (from Lindenfield's operations reporting, six months after go-live)
- 64% of paper claims now flow through without manual keying. Source: intake platform audit log.
- Average intake time fell from 11 days to 3 days.

CLIENT INTERVIEW — Marcus Bell, Director of Claims Operations (notes)
"The backlog used to be a fact of life. Now it is an exception we can see coming."

NOT FOR PUBLICATION
- One vendor integration was replaced mid-project after a security review; do not mention externally.
